question: How is the Shakta mode described in relation to the inner faculties and maya?
premises: The Shakta mode involves mind, intellect, thought, and ego-making.
What appears as will and so on is maya-made in form, though not ultimately so in reality.
inference: Therefore the Shakta mode works through conceptual inner faculties while reinterpreting their maya-bound appearance.
uncertainties: The compound cetodhī-manohaṃkṛti compresses several inner functions; the gloss follows the standard grouping.
plain_english: Now the Shakta mode is described: mind, intellect, thought, and ego-making operate clearly with conceptuality, and what appears as will and so on is maya-made in form, though in reality otherwise.
